content: {"summary":"All card payments failed after midnight on 2025‑01‑14 because the client TLS certificate (CPX‑E600) used by both card‑processor‑proxy pods expired at 00:00 UTC and was subsequently replaced with a new certificate via a CSR, secret update, and pod restart.","likely_cause":"Expiration of the card‑processor‑proxy client certificate (CPX‑E600) caused TLS handshake failures.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"The client certificate CPX‑E600 expired at 00:00 UTC on 2025‑01‑14.","evidence_ids":["RB-023#4","RB-023#2"],"quote":"Expired 00:00 UTC; `CPX-E600` and `PAYAPI-E1107` on every card payment."},{"text":"Both proxy pods began failing fast with CPX‑E600 errors, causing all payments to fail.","evidence_ids":["RB-023#1"],"quote":"both pods from one exact minute, every call failing fast"},{"text":"The expired certificate was replaced by generating a new key/CSR, uploading it, updating the Kubernetes secret, and restarting the deployment.","evidence_ids":["RB-023#3","RB-023#4"],"quote":"replace the Secret, then restart: the proxy only reads it at start."}],"next_checks":["Verify the current notAfter date of the card‑processor‑client‑tls secret","Confirm the secret was successfully updated and pods have restarted","Ensure alerts are configured for certificate expiry (30‑day and 7‑day warnings)","Check rollout status to confirm no pods are still using the expired cert"]}
